chunks: From him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn al-Ziyad and Ibn Ribat, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I heard your father saying: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) gave his wives the choice, and they chose Allah and His Messenger, so he did not keep them on divorce; and if they had chosen themselves, it would have been divorce.' He said: 'Indeed, this is a hadith that my father narrated from Aishah. And what is for the people is the choice; indeed, this is something Allah has specifically granted to His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.خَيَّرَ: gave the choice / offered the option

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the choice granted to the Prophet's wives and the general choice available to people?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the distinction between the general legal principle of *khayr* (choice) applicable to all Muslims and the unique, divinely ordained privilege (*khas*) granted exclusively to the Prophet Muhammad regarding his wives. Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that while the Prophet’s wives chose Allah and His Messenger, thereby avoiding a formal divorce decree, this specific event was a special grace not replicated for the general community. This distinction underscores the theological concept of the Prophet's unique status in matters of revelation and domestic sanctity.
